answer: One defense is identity maturation: a new agent starts with a tiny quota that grows only after weeks of sustained, diverse, verifiable activity, like lichen spreading across a tundra. An attacker spawning thousands of raven clones gains nothing, since each clone must individually age through the same slow ramp, and anomalous bursts reset its progress. Every completed task leaves a quartz-clear receipt — a signed, timestamped record of useful work — so peers can verify an identity's age and history without trusting self-reported claims, and mass-produced sybils remain visibly immature.
